clue.text: Theatrical 12/17/19/28 constructing meagre plot for development

indicators.note: constructing means building something new out of the word meagre, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a plot where flowers and vegetables are grown and developed, a bed of cultivated ground

explanation.surface: A dramatist works a thin storyline up into something fuller.
explanation.walkthrough: 12/17/19/28 read together spell CANTABRIGIAN, someone from Cambridge; the theme is Cambridge Footlights performers. 'constructing' turns MEAGRE into GRAEME.
explanation.definitionFit: Graeme Garden, of The Goodies, was a Cambridge Footlights performer, so a theatrical Cambridge man.

clue.text: Georgia, French girl comes across price for DIY material?

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: the girl comes across, i.e. sits between, the two letters standing for price

parts.note: fille is French for girl

explanation.surface: A girl from Georgia meets a French one and stumbles on a price tag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes across' puts FILLE between P and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Gap filler is a putty or paste a home decorator uses to plug holes, so a do-it-yourself product.

clue.text: Carry out woolly thing wrapped in a fleece

indicators.note: the ram is enclosed by the word for fleece, so it goes inside

parts.note: to fleece someone is to swindle them, to con them
a tup is a ram, an animal covered in wool

explanation.surface: Something woolly is bundled up in a sheepskin and carried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like sheep's wool, matching 'woolly', but it is the verb meaning to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To act upon advice or orders is to carry them out, put them into effect.

clue.text: Horse hurt tail in fence

parts.note: to mar is to damage or hurt

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, here taken from fence

explanation.surface: A horse injured its tail jumping a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare is a female horse, so an example of the general term.

clue.text: Theatrical 12/17/19/28 unproductive when Bill's in? No way

indicators.note: No way asks for the letters for way to be removed
Bill's in means the police letters are put inside the word for unproductive

parts.note: sterile land or effort produces nothing
the Old Bill is British slang for the police; CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch
ST, street, is a common crossword abbreviation for a way

explanation.surface: An idle performer is told nothing will happen while the police are around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill's in' puts CID into STERILE, giving STERICIDLE; 'No way' then drops ST. The Old Bill is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Idle of Monty Python began in the Cambridge Footlights, so he is a Cambridge-educated performer.

clue.text: He scored from cross, when losing first home international

indicators.note: losing first means the opening letter of cross is dropped

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A footballer scores from a cross, though his side lost the first home international.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He scored' looks like football, but means composed music.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini composed operas such as The Barber of Seville, and a composer writes scores.

clue.text: Drivers reveal coats in conversation?

indicators.note: in conversation signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: to reveal coats is to show furs

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a chat with drivers will expose what they wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, SHOW FURS matches the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chauffeurs are paid drivers of private cars.

clue.text: Glance at frills of ultrashort dress

parts.note: a decko (or dekko) is informal British slang for a quick look

indicators.note: frills are edges, so the outer letters of ultrashort are taken

explanation.surface: Someone eyes the ruffled hem of a very short dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' is a verb here. DECKO is slang from Hindi for a look.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck out is to adorn or dress up, in fine clothes or decorations.

clue.text: He painted aquatic birds top to bottom

indicators.note: in a down entry the top letter is moved to the bottom, the end of the word

parts.note: terns are seabirds

explanation.surface: An artist painted waterbirds from head to foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German Surrealist painter.

clue.text: Clips from Beatles' stadium venue extremely raucous

parts.note: Shea Stadium in New York hosted a famous Beatles concert in 1965

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, of raucous

explanation.surface: Clips from the Beatles' stadium gig were extremely noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clips' suggests film footage, but it is the verb for cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Shears are cutting tools, and a person who clips a hedge or a fleece shears it.

clue.text: Theatrical 12/17/19/28 preferred regulars to hear fiddle

parts.note: a pet project or pet subject is a favourite, preferred one

indicators.note: regulars takes every other letter of hear, the second and fourth

parts.note: to falsify accounts, as in fiddling the books, is to doctor them

explanation.surface: A performer would rather listen to a violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' looks like the violin but means to falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Cook was a star of the Cambridge Footlights and Beyond the Fringe.

clue.text: Lily's ¾ socks appreciated

indicators.note: three quarters keeps three of the four letters of the word for socks, dropping the last

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks
ta is British informal for thank you, expressing appreciation

explanation.surface: Lily has been grateful for most of a pair of socks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily' looks like a girl's name; it is the plant group.
explanation.definitionFit: The hosta, or plantain lily, is a shade-loving garden plant once classed in the lily family.

clue.text: Prison toilet

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are slang uses of the same short word for a container.

clue.text: One's pony outwardly looking game

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S, written IS

indicators.note: outwardly takes the outside letters of pony

explanation.surface: A child's pony appears to be playing.
explanation.definitionFit: I spy is a children's guessing game played by looking around for objects.

clue.text: Theatrical 12/17/19/28 eager for changes after director vacated seat

indicators.note: after places the eager word after the letter for director

parts.note: avid means eager

indicators.note: changes asks for the letters of for to be rearranged
vacated empties seat of its middle, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: An actor is keen for a new arrangement once the director leaves his chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns FOR into FRO; 'vacated' leaves ST from SEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: David Frost appeared with the Cambridge Footlights before his broadcasting career.

clue.text: Imagined business to be ruined in court after one is sacked

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: is sacked means the letter for one is dismissed from the word

parts.note: something injured is damaged, ruined
I is the Roman numeral for one
to be up before a judge is to be in court

explanation.surface: A firm faces ruin in court once one employee is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is sacked' drops I from INJURED, leaving NJURED.
explanation.definitionFit: To conjure up a picture is to call it to mind, to imagine it.

clue.text: Swimmer utilising a long vessel during practice

indicators.note: utilising, putting to new use, signals that the letters of a long are reworked
the vessel comes during, inside, the word for practice

parts.note: use is custom or practice
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: A swimmer trains with a long boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utilising' is a loose anagram signal: the letters of A LONG are put to new use. 'during' puts the vessel inside the word for practice.
explanation.definitionFit: The langoustine is a small lobster, a creature that swims, so humorously a swimmer.

clue.text: High-flyer's return ticket

indicators.note: return asks for the flying creature's letters to be read backwards

parts.note: a bat is a flying mammal, a creature of the night skies

explanation.surface: A frequent flyer buys a return ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyer' suggests a successful person; it is a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tab is a bill or account, a ticket for what is owed.

clue.text: Analyse some of bird feathers found around river

indicators.note: found around means the beak is placed around the river letter

parts.note: a beak is part of a bird
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Bird feathers are found lying near a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To break down figures is to divide them into parts and examine them.

clue.text: Some pumping iron returned equipment

indicators.note: returned means those letters are read backwards
some takes part of the letters of pumping iron

explanation.surface: A weightlifter takes back his gym kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rig is apparatus or gear set up for a job, such as a drilling rig.

clue.text: Turned up, for example, with money to enter

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: EG abbreviates the Latin exempli gratia, for example
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone shows up, say, with cash to get in.
explanation.definitionFit: To get into a building is to enter it.

clue.text: Theatrical 12/17/19/28 of north of resort in summer month

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the month

parts.note: June is a summer month

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so the letters of of north are sorted again

explanation.surface: A performer from up north appears at a seaside town in summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a seaside town; read it as 're-sort', rearranging OF NORTH, which then sits inside the month after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Fortune was a satirist who came through the Cambridge Footlights.

clue.text: Drake's cry of delight, hot for new duck?

indicators.note: hot for new means the letter for hot replaces the letter for new

parts.note: heaven is bliss, delight
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A male duck quacks with joy and someone suggests a fresh duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drake' is Sir Francis Drake, the sailor, not a male duck. 'for' swaps N for H in HEAVENO.
explanation.definitionFit: Heave-ho is the traditional cry of sailors hauling ropes, such as Drake's crew.

clue.text: Meat dish is horse, not a sausage, soaked in oil

indicators.note: soaked in places the pieces inside the word for oil

parts.note: fat is oily grease used in cooking
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse
not a sausage is British slang for nothing at all, O

explanation.surface: A dish is said to be horsemeat, no sausage, swimming in oil.
explanation.walkthrough: A faggot is a British meatball of offal.
explanation.definitionFit: Faggots are baked balls of chopped liver and other offal, a traditional British meal.

clue.text: Uranium study, attained in retreat, not acknowledged

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

indicators.note: in retreat means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study
won means gained, attained

explanation.surface: A uranium researcher's gains go unrecognised while he is on retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unowned is not claimed or admitted to by anyone, so disowned.

clue.text: Great sprawling university probes fee for measuring instrument

indicators.note: probes means these letters push into the word for fee

parts.note: a wage is a payment, a fee

indicators.note: sprawling means the letters of great are spread out in a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'sprawling' makes ATERG; with U it goes inside WAGE after W.
explanation.definitionFit: A water gauge is an instrument showing the level of water in a tank or boiler.

clue.text: Rubbish heard in middle of ship

indicators.note: heard means the word for rubbish is spoken, giving one that sounds identical

parts.note: waste is rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone hears garbage in the centre of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The waist of a ship is the central part of the upper deck, between forecastle and quarterdeck.
